A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TrigFlow/sCM research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material and renumbered tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original sCT/sCD experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, including benchmark scores, training ablations, scaling analyses, and generated samples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds an sCT-versus-ECT convergence comparison in Appendix E.3 and Table 3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 corrects the discrete-time training target from a continuous-derivative expression to cos(t)Δθ−(xt,t,t′,r). This aligns the pseudocode with the finite-difference objective already defined in v1 Appendix E.1. The core continuous-time architecture, objective, sampling procedure, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate unconditional CIFAR-10 generation and class-conditional ImageNet generation at 64×64 and 512×512. The added ECT comparison uses existing CIFAR-10 coverage; no new dataset, domain, or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds OT-CFM to the CIFAR-10 comparison and removes BOOT (LPIPS). ECT, already included in both versions' benchmark table, also participates in the new Appendix E.3 convergence comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix E.3 introduces a controlled ECT comparison using matching DDPM++ architecture, dropout 0.20, and batch size 128, with evaluations at 100k, 200k, and 400k iterations. Its sCT proposal parameters are Pmean=-1.0 and Pstd=1.8. This is a separate setup from the retained main CIFAR-10 experiment, whose batch size is 512 and Pstd is 1.4.

E4.justification: The new Appendix E.3 examines convergence against ECT under matched configurations. Figure 5(b) also revises the adaptive-weighting ablation by swapping the two-step curve assignments, reversing their late-training ordering. The other stability, discretization, scaling, and VSD analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these results. The new convergence table continues point-estimate FID reporting; discussion of gradient variance concerns optimization rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes one-step CIFAR-10 sCT FID from 2.97 to 2.85, adds OT-CFM at 3.57, and removes BOOT at 4.38. New Table 3 reports sCT FIDs 3.97/3.51/3.09 versus ECT's 4.54/3.86/3.60 at 100k/200k/400k iterations under its separate setup. Figure 5(b) now favors adaptive weighting for later two-step results. Headline two-step scores and retained appendix result tables are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 corrects coefficient errors within the existing derivation, including alpha/sigma substitutions in Equations 11 and 13–18 and changing Equation 22's weighting from cos² to sin². Section 3 corrects cout to -σd sin(t), and Appendix D restores a missing gradient symbol. The underlying framework and formal assumptions are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: unifying parameterizations through TrigFlow, stabilizing continuous-time consistency models, scaling to 1.5 billion parameters, and achieving the same headline two-step FIDs.

C2.justification: The new Discussions and Limitations section substantially expands interpretation and applicability boundaries. It proposes latent-space conditioning as an explanation for weaker sCT performance, discusses JVP computation costs, and acknowledges artifacts, FID's limitations, unvalidated higher-resolution/video scaling, architecture constraints, and dependence on teacher models. Section 4.2 also calls warmup optional, although its ensuing statement refers ambiguously to tangent normalization.

D1.justification: Appendix E.3 supplies implementation details for the added comparison, including DDPM++ without AdaGN, dropout, batch size, and proposal-distribution parameters. Algorithm 2's correction improves consistency of the implementation instructions. Existing Appendix G settings, preprocessing instructions, and resource references are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tong et al. (2023) on minibatch optimal transport and Kornilov et al. (2024) on optimal flow matching, while removing Gu et al. (2023) on BOOT. The ECT comparison adds evidence concerning an already cited competitor; the broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 adds Discussions and Limitations and Appendix E.3, removes acknowledgements, distinguishes diffusion-model notation from consistency-model notation, and makes localized wording edits. The main section sequence and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 3, revises Table 1's rows, and redraws Figure 5(b), including its styling and curve assignments. Conference headers and reflow shift several figures, tables, and algorithms. The remaining plotted content and generated-image galleries are retained.

improvement.justification: Corrected TrigFlow algebra and discrete-time pseudocode improve internal consistency, while the controlled ECT comparison and substantive limitations strengthen the evidence and its qualification. These gains are limited by an unexplained curve reassignment in Figure 5(b) and a new Section 4.2 statement that normalization does not affect sample quality, which conflicts with Figure 5(a). Overall, v2 improves the paper modestly while retaining its main study and claims.
